EWS-FLI1 occupies GGAA microsatellite repeats and canonical ETS sites, creating de novo enhancers while repressing other enhancer classes.

EWS-FLI1 recruits NuRD-associated HDAC and LSD1 activities for transcriptional repression; the separate CHD4 survival dependency does not establish that CHD4 acts through EWS-FLI1 target-gene regulation.
EWS-FLI1 directly activates ATF4 and metabolic stress-response programs.
High-output transcription and defective damage-associated transcriptional control promote R-loop accumulation and replication stress.
In TOP1-poison-treated Ewing cells, EWS-FLI1 binds DHX9 and interferes with resolution of drug-induced R-loops.
The fusion protein is subject to dosage control and its abundance changes the transcriptional state.
EWS-FLI1 directly activates SLFN11 transcription.
EWS-FLI1 increases USP1 expression and thereby supports survivin-dependent stress tolerance.
Fusion expression perturbs faithful POLQ splicing in the reported cellular models; this preprint-derived edge is provisional.

Fusion binding at the EZH2 promoter induces expression.
BAF retargeting supports tumor-specific enhancer activation downstream of EWS-FLI1 occupancy.
Dynamic EWS-FLI1 hubs concentrate the fusion on chromatin and tune enhancer activation at GGAA microsatellites.
EWS-FLI1 establishes super-enhancers for KLF15, TCF4, and NKX2-2, building an autoregulatory transcription-factor circuit.
Aberrant enhancer repression suppresses mesenchymal lineage regulators.
A fusion-created GGAA enhancer activates the HOXD locus.
ETV6 competition modulates EWS-FLI1 occupancy and output at short GGAA microsatellite enhancers.
ETV6 restrains excessive fusion activity and maintains a viable undifferentiated tumor state. ETV6 loss instead induces differentiation or cellular stress and suppresses growth in preclinical models.
Germline GGAA repeat length and purity alter the strength of EWS-FLI1 neo-enhancer formation at susceptible loci.
Susceptibility-locus enhancer activation can increase expression of proliferation-associated transcriptional regulators.
NuRD/LSD1/HDAC-mediated repression helps EWS-FLI1 maintain an immature, transformed state.
NuRD-associated repression of tumor-suppressive loci contributes to the transformed phenotype. This edge refers to transcriptional repression, not the separate CHD4 DNA-damage buffering mechanism.
Core regulatory transcription factors sustain proliferation and oncogenic signaling pathways in Ewing sarcoma cells.
Core regulatory circuitry reinforces the undifferentiated tumor state.
Fusion-driven metabolic rewiring supports biomass production, redox state, and survival in rapidly proliferating tumor cells.
Transcription-associated BRCA1 retention can impair repair availability in the tested cellular context.

STAG2/cohesin status changes enhancer-promoter communication at long EWS-FLI1-bound GGAA repeats and rewires enhancer output.
STAG2 loss can promote an aggressive, metastasis-prone transcriptional state.
Sustained proliferation and impaired differentiation produce the expanding local tumor mass.

Fusion dosage changes can contribute to mesenchymal plasticity, but dosage is not the sole determinant of the observed hybrid programs.

USP1-dependent survivin stabilization suppresses stress-associated apoptosis.
Metabolic adaptation can support survival under genotoxic therapy in SLFN11-deficient cellular models.
PARP1 supports the broader fusion transcriptional program; a specific requirement at every GGAA enhancer has not been demonstrated.
Stromal cytokine signaling modifies tumor-cell survival and drug response in a tissue-engineered model.
Destructive local tumor growth can produce pain; the precise nociceptive pathway is not inferred from a specific molecular study.

edges.description: Tests lineage-specific fusion tolerance and transformation.
Tests tumorigenicity of an experimentally permissive progenitor state.

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1 and menin converge on ATF4 to activate a serine synthesis pathway transcriptional program. EWS-FLI1 also upregulates glutamine uptake and one-carbon cycle genes, linking fusion-driven transcription to biosynthetic metabolism, redox state, and survival.

biological_processes: generation of precursor metabolites and energy

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 and Menin Converge to Regulate ATF4 Activity in Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: We identified and validated an EWS-FLI1 binding site at the ATF4 promoter, indicating that the fusion can directly activate ATF4 transcription.

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 reprograms the metabolism of Ewing sarcoma cells via positive regulation of glutamine import and serine-glycine biosynthesis.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that EWS-FLI1 positively regulates the expression of proteins required for serine-glycine biosynthesis and uptake of the alternative nutrient source glutamine.

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 reprograms the metabolism of Ewing sarcoma cells via positive regulation of glutamine import and serine-glycine biosynthesis.
evidence.snippet: In summary, our study demonstrates that EWS-FLI1 reprograms the metabolism of EWS cells and that serine-glycine metabolism or glutamine uptake are potential targetable vulnerabilities in this tumor type.

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1 uses the EWSR1 low-complexity/prion-like domain to retarget BRG1/BRM-associated factor (BAF/SWI-SNF) chromatin-remodeling complexes to tumor-specific enhancers. This neomorphic recruitment depends on tyrosine residues linked to phase-transition behavior of the EWSR1 domain and helps establish oncogenic enhancer activity.

evidence.reference_title: Cancer-Specific Retargeting of BAF Complexes by a Prion-like Domain.
evidence.snippet: In Ewing sarcoma, we find that the BAF complex is recruited by the EWS-FLI1 fusion protein to tumor-specific enhancers and contributes to target gene activation.

evidence.reference_title: Cancer-Specific Retargeting of BAF Complexes by a Prion-like Domain.
evidence.snippet: This process is a neomorphic property of EWS-FLI1 compared to wild-type FLI1 and depends on tyrosine residues that are necessary for phase transitions of the EWSR1 prion-like domain.

nodes.description: A BARD1-variant patient-derived Ewing cell line and BARD1-depletion experiments show enhanced sensitivity to PARP inhibition and radiation. BARD1 loss can increase GBP1 expression, which contributes to damage-induced apoptosis in the tested cells. Other signals also induce GBP1, so expression is not a specific BARD1-loss marker. This is a bounded experimental modifier of treatment response; neither disease-wide BARD1 prevalence, penetrant inherited Ewing susceptibility nor a validated clinical predictive biomarker is established.

evidence.reference_title: BRCA1-associated RING domain-1 (BARD1) loss and GBP1 expression enhance sensitivity to DNA damage in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that PSaRC318 cells, a novel patient-derived cell line harboring a pathogenic BARD1 variant, are sensitive to PARP inhibition and by testing the effect of BARD1 depletion in additional Ewing sarcoma cell lines, we confirm that BARD1 loss enhances cell sensitivity to PARP inhibition plus radiation.

evidence.reference_title: BRCA1-associated RING domain-1 (BARD1) loss and GBP1 expression enhance sensitivity to DNA damage in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that GBP1 contributes to the enhanced sensitivity of BARD1 deficient Ewing cells to DNA damage.

experimental_models.description: Tests BARD1 depletion and the contribution of GBP1 to PARP-inhibitor or radiation-associated apoptosis.
experimental_models.name: BARD1-variant PSaRC318 and BARD1-depleted Ewing cells

nodes.description: PSaRC318 derives from one patient with a germline pathogenic BARD1 variant. BARD1 depletion in other Ewing lines and GBP1 knockdown test the cellular contribution to damage sensitivity. These interventions do not establish treatment benefit in patients.
nodes.id: BARD1-variant PSaRC318 and BARD1-depleted Ewing cells

evidence.reference_title: BRCA1-associated RING domain-1 (BARD1) loss and GBP1 expression enhance sensitivity to DNA damage in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that PSaRC318 cells, a novel patient-derived cell line harboring a pathogenic BARD1 variant, are sensitive to PARP inhibition and by testing the effect of BARD1 depletion in additional Ewing sarcoma cell lines, we confirm that BARD1 loss enhances cell sensitivity to PARP inhibition plus radiation.

evidence.reference_title: BRCA1-associated RING domain-1 (BARD1) loss and GBP1 expression enhance sensitivity to DNA damage in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that GBP1 contributes to the enhanced sensitivity of BARD1 deficient Ewing cells to DNA damage.

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1 and its downstream transcriptional circuitry repress mesenchymal lineage regulators, maintaining Ewing sarcoma cells in an immature, proliferative state. This mechanism is linked to the unresolved cell-of-origin question because only some early progenitor contexts tolerate EWS-FLI1 and progress toward an Ewing-like state.

evidence.reference_title: EWS/FLI utilizes NKX2-2 to repress mesenchymal features of Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Here we provide evidence that NKX2-2 mediates the EWS/FLI-controlled block of mesenchymal features.

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 utilizes divergent chromatin remodeling mechanisms to directly activate or repress enhancer elements in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: These divergent chromatin-remodeling patterns repress tumor suppressors and mesenchymal lineage regulators while activating oncogenes and potential therapeutic targets, such as the kinase VRK1.

nodes.description: Localized bone pain is a common presenting symptom of osseous disease, sometimes intermittent or initially attributed to strain. Frequency varies with age, site and ascertainment; the cited 75.3% estimate is from a single-center adult cohort, not a universal pediatric estimate.

evidence.reference_title: Outcomes of Adult Ewing Sarcoma Treated with Multimodality Therapy: A Single-Institute Experience.
evidence.snippet: Pain (75.3%) was the most common symptom at presentation.

nodes.description: CHD4/NuRD maintains global chromatin structure and limits spontaneous DNA damage in Ewing cells. Despite colocalization with EWS-FLI1 at enhancers, the reported survival effect did not operate by changing EWS-FLI1 activity or its oncogenic expression program. CHD4 loss causes apoptosis and increases sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents; combined CHD4 depletion and olaparib suppressed xenograft growth.

evidence.reference_title: The Chromatin Remodeler CHD4 Sustains Ewing Sarcoma Cell Survival by Controlling Global Chromatin Architecture.
evidence.snippet: Although CHD4 and NuRD colocalized with EWS-FLI1 at enhancers and super-enhancers, CHD4 promoted Ewing sarcoma cell survival not by modulating EWS-FLI1 activity and its oncogenic gene expression program but by regulating chromatin structure.

evidence.reference_title: The Chromatin Remodeler CHD4 Sustains Ewing Sarcoma Cell Survival by Controlling Global Chromatin Architecture.
evidence.snippet: CHD4 depletion led to a global increase in DNA accessibility and induction of spontaneous DNA damage, resulting in an increased susceptibility to DNA-damaging agents.

nodes.description: Enrichment of BRCA1 at elongating transcription machinery can reduce its availability for damage repair in Ewing cell models. Other experiments found no apparent HR defect and attributed PARP sensitivity to trapped PARP-DNA complexes. These observations constrain the scope of an HR-deficiency model rather than establishing either uniform HR proficiency or uniform clinical BRCAness. PARP trapping and context-dependent HR impairment can coexist.

biological_processes: double-strand break repair via homologous recombination

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 increases transcription to cause R-loops and block BRCA1 repair in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: In addition, homologous recombination is impaired in Ewing sarcoma owing to an enriched interaction between BRCA1 and the elongating transcription machinery.

evidence.reference_title: Combinations of PARP Inhibitors with Temozolomide Drive PARP1 Trapping and Apoptosis in Ewing's Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that PARP inhibitor sensitivity in Ewing's sarcoma cells is not through an apparent defect in DNA repair by HR, but through hypersensitivity to trapped PARP1-DNA complexes.

experimental_models.description: Measures altered BRCA1 expression, localization and damage-response phosphorylation alongside defective DNA repair in comet assays after EWS-FLI1 expression.
experimental_models.name: Human embryonic mesenchymal stem cell EWS-FLI1 transformation model

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1 activates super-enhancers controlling a core regulatory circuitry composed of transcription factors including KLF15, TCF4, and NKX2-2. These factors reinforce their own and each other's regulatory elements and cooperate with EWS-FLI1 to sustain proliferation, survival signaling, and the Ewing transcriptional state.

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 regulates and cooperates with core regulatory circuitry in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Epigenomic analyses demonstrate that EWS-FLI1, the primary fusion driver for this cancer, directly establishes super-enhancers of each of these three TFs to activate their transcription.

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 regulates and cooperates with core regulatory circuitry in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Functionally, CRC factors contribute significantly to cell proliferation of Ewing sarcoma both in vitro and in vivo.

nodes.description: Following topoisomerase I poison exposure, EWS-FLI1 sequesters DHX9 helicase and prevents resolution of drug-induced R-loops. Excess DHX9 or reduced fusion expression confers SN-38 resistance independent of measured proliferation and global transcription rates. This supports a protein-interaction contribution under topoisomerase stress, without proving complete independence from transcription or untreated tumor initiation.

evidence.reference_title: EWS::FLI1-DHX9 interaction promotes Ewing sarcoma sensitivity to DNA topoisomerase 1 poisons by altering R-loop metabolism.
evidence.snippet: We discovered that EWS::FLI1 prevents the resolution of R-loops induced by these drugs via sequestering DHX9 helicase, ultimately resulting in R-loop accumulation, replication stress, and genome instability.

nodes.description: The bifunctional compound kt-3283 has preclinical activity in Ewing cells and spheroids. It inhibits PARP1/2 and HDAC enzymes; these observations do not establish direct CHD4 inhibition or clinical efficacy.

evidence.reference_title: A Bifunctional PARP-HDAC Inhibitor with Activity in Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report the concept and characterization of a novel bifunctional PARPi (kt-3283) with dual activity toward PARP1/2 and HDAC enzymes in Ewing sarcoma cells.

nodes.description: ETV6 is a native ETS-family factor that competes with EWS-FLI1 at select short GGAA-repeat elements. This counter-regulatory layer restrains part of the enhanceropathy, and forced ETV6 degradation can paradoxically increase EWS-FLI1 transcriptional stress and tumor cell death.

evidence.reference_title: ETV6 dependency in Ewing sarcoma by antagonism of EWS-FLI1-mediated enhancer activation.
evidence.snippet: Using biochemical assays and epigenomics, we show that ETV6 competes with EWS-FLI1 for binding to select DNA elements enriched for short GGAA repeat sequences.

evidence.reference_title: (GGAA)(3)-Based TF-PROTACs Enable Targeted Degradation of ETV6 to Inhibit Ewing Sarcoma Growth.
evidence.snippet: Recent studies identified ETV6 as a vulnerability in Ewing sarcoma, where it competes with EWS::FLI1 at short GGAA repeats to restrain EWS::FLI1 function.

evidence.reference_title: ETV6 dependency in Ewing sarcoma by antagonism of EWS-FLI1-mediated enhancer activation.
evidence.snippet: Upon inactivating ETV6, EWS-FLI1 overtakes and hyper-activates these cis-elements to promote mesenchymal differentiation, with SOX11 being a key downstream target.

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1 low-complexity-domain interactions support GGAA-associated transcription within a narrow interaction-strength optimum. A 2026 bioRxiv preprint reports endogenous dynamic sub-diffraction hubs that dissolve before macroscopic liquid-liquid phase separation. This is a provisional refinement of the published interaction-optimum model, not evidence that macroscopic condensates are required for oncogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: Dynamic regulation of endogenous transcription factor hubs at single-molecule resolution.
evidence.snippet: We found that endogenous EWS::FLI1 forms dynamic, sub-diffraction-limit hubs with mechanisms of dissolution that prevent the hubs from achieving macroscopic liquid-liquid phase separation.

evidence.reference_title: Tuning levels of low-complexity domain interactions to modulate endogenous oncogenic transcription.
evidence.snippet: Quantitative single-cell and single-molecule imaging reveals that the oncogenic TF EWS::FLI1 requires a narrow optimum of LCD-LCD interactions to activate its target genes associated with GGAA microsatellites.

nodes.description: Fusion abundance and low-complexity-domain interaction strength are related but distinct control variables. TRIM8-mediated turnover prevents toxic fusion accumulation. Engineered graded depletion and restoration of endogenous EWS-FLI1 produce persistent transcriptional changes and increased metastatic behavior at intermediate depletion in preclinical models. This does not establish a clinical hazard of a particular inhibitor dose.

evidence.reference_title: TRIM8 modulates the EWS/FLI oncoprotein to promote survival in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, TRIM8 knockout led to an increase in EWS/FLI protein levels that was not tolerated.

evidence.reference_title: Modelling EWS::FLI1 protein fluctuations reveal determinants of tumor plasticity in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Strikingly, modest EF depletion promoted a pro-metastatic phenotype that diminished upon near-complete EF loss, revealing a paradoxical effect of submaximal EF inhibition.

nodes.description: The t(11;22)(q24;q12) translocation fuses the EWS gene (EWSR1) on chromosome 22 with the FLI1 gene on chromosome 11. The resulting EWS-FLI1 protein functions as an aberrant FET-ETS transcription factor. It is the truncal driver of most Ewing sarcomas, but its oncogenic effect depends on a permissive developmental cell state and on downstream enhancer, transcriptional, metabolic, and DNA damage-response programs.

biological_processes: positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 and Menin Converge to Regulate ATF4 Activity in Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Ewing sarcomas are driven by EWS-ETS fusions, most commonly EWS-FLI1, which promotes widespread metabolic reprogramming, including activation of serine biosynthesis.

evidence.reference_title: The Biology of Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: It is associated in 85% of cases with the t(11;22)(q24:q12) chromosomal translocation that generates fusion of the 5' segment of the EWS gene with the 3' segment of the ETS family gene FLI-1.

evidence.reference_title: The Biology of Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: The resulting EWS-FLI-1 fusion protein is believed to behave as an aberrant transcriptional activator that contributes to ESFT development by altering the expression of its target genes in a permissive cellular environment.

experimental_models.name: Patient-derived Ewing sarcoma culture panel

experimental_models.name: Human embryonic mesenchymal stem cell EWS-FLI1 transformation model

nodes.description: Tests tumorigenicity of engineered early human mesenchymal cells. The implanted cell origin is known, but this does not trace spontaneous human disease.

evidence.reference_title: EWS::FLI1 expression in human embryonic mesenchymal stem cells leads to transcriptional reprograming, defective DNA damage repair and Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Xenografting of EWS::FLI1-transduced heMSCs results in the formation of tumors expressing characteristic ES markers.

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1 induces EZH2, which contributes to repression of differentiation-associated genes and maintenance of an undifferentiated state. Genetic depletion impairs clonogenicity and tumorigenicity in preclinical systems. This dependency is distinct from the heterogeneous PRC2 changes following STAG2 loss and does not imply that every Ewing tumor will respond to an EZH2 inhibitor.

evidence.reference_title: EZH2 is a mediator of EWS/FLI1 driven tumor growth and metastasis blocking endothelial and neuro-ectodermal differentiation.
evidence.snippet: Here, we found EWS/FLI1 bound to the EZH2 promoter in vivo, and induced EZH2 expression in ET and mesenchymal stem cells.

evidence.reference_title: EZH2 is a mediator of EWS/FLI1 driven tumor growth and metastasis blocking endothelial and neuro-ectodermal differentiation.
evidence.snippet: Subsequent microarray analysis of EZH2 knock down, HDAC-inhibitor treatment and confirmation in independent assays revealed an undifferentiated phenotype maintained by EZH2 in ET.

nodes.description: Tumor organoids are part of the current Ewing sarcoma preclinical model landscape and provide a non-animal 3D system for therapy evaluation and mechanism-focused modeling alongside cell lines and xenografts.
nodes.id: Ewing sarcoma tumor organoid model systems

evidence.reference_title: Advancing Preclinical Biology for Ewing Sarcoma: An International Effort.
evidence.snippet: Through an international collaborative effort between the Children's Oncology Group Bone Tumor Committee and the Euro Ewing Consortium, we review the current landscape of preclinical modeling used in Ewing sarcoma research encompassing both in vitro (cell lines and tumor organoids) and in vivo (mouse and nonmammalian xenografts) model systems.

nodes.description: Flow-perfusion 3D scaffold cocultures combine Ewing sarcoma cells with mesenchymal stromal cells under biomechanical stimulation, enabling controlled testing of tumor-stroma signaling, IGF-1R/STAT3 biology, and drug-resistance mechanisms that are absent from standard monolayer systems.

evidence.reference_title: Modeling Stroma-Induced Drug Resistance in a Tissue-Engineered Tumor Model of Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that these same biophysical cues-modeled by coculturing ES cells and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in 3D scaffolds within a flow perfusion bioreactor-activate interleukin-6 and transcription factor Stat3.

evidence.reference_title: Flow perfusion effects on three-dimensional culture and drug sensitivity of Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: To address this issue, we cultured Ewing sarcoma (ES) cells on electrospun poly(ε-caprolactone) 3D scaffolds within a flow perfusion bioreactor.

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1 binds GGAA microsatellite repeats and canonical ETS motifs, remodeling the enhancer landscape. At GGAA repeats, multimeric EWS-FLI1 opens chromatin and creates de novo enhancers that contact target promoters; at conserved ETS enhancers, EWS-FLI1 can displace wild-type ETS factors and repress tumor suppressor and lineage-regulatory programs.

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 utilizes divergent chromatin remodeling mechanisms to directly activate or repress enhancer elements in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: We find that EWS-FLI1 reprograms gene regulatory circuits in Ewing sarcoma by directly inducing or repressing enhancers.

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 utilizes divergent chromatin remodeling mechanisms to directly activate or repress enhancer elements in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: At GGAA repeat elements, which lack evolutionary conservation and regulatory potential in other cell types, EWS-FLI1 multimers induce chromatin opening and create de novo enhancers that physically interact with target promoters.

evidence.reference_title: Tumor-specific retargeting of an oncogenic transcription factor chimera results in dysregulation of chromatin and transcription.
evidence.snippet: We found that in tumor cells, EWS-FLI targets regions of the genome distinct from FLI1, despite identical DNA-binding domains.

evidence.reference_title: Tumor-specific retargeting of an oncogenic transcription factor chimera results in dysregulation of chromatin and transcription.
evidence.snippet: Expression of EWS-FLI results in nucleosome depletion at targeted sites, whereas silencing of EWS-FLI in tumor cells restored nucleosome occupancy.

evidence.reference_title: STAG2 loss amplifies EWS-FLI1-driven microsatellite enhancer activity promoting Ewing sarcoma aggressiveness.
evidence.snippet: EWS-FLI1 engages GGAA microsatellite repeats to form de novo enhancers that activate oncogenic transcriptional programs essential for tumorigenesis.

evidence.reference_title: DNA methylation heterogeneity defines a disease spectrum in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: We observed consistent DNA hypomethylation at enhancers regulated by the disease-defining EWS-FLI1 fusion protein, thus establishing epigenomic enhancer reprogramming as a ubiquitous and characteristic feature of Ewing sarcoma.

nodes.description: Germline variation in GGAA microsatellite architecture can determine how strongly the acquired EWS-FLI1 fusion converts a locus into a neo-enhancer. At EGR2 and RREB1 susceptibility loci, longer or newly contiguous GGAA repeat alleles increase EWS-FLI1 binding and enhancer output, linking inherited repeat length to the somatic enhanceropathy and proliferative transcriptional programs.

evidence.reference_title: Chimeric EWSR1-FLI1 regulates the Ewing sarcoma susceptibility gene EGR2 via a GGAA microsatellite.
evidence.snippet: At rs79965208, the A risk allele connected adjacent GGAA repeats by converting an interspaced GGAT motif into a GGAA motif, thereby increasing the number of consecutive GGAA motifs and thus the EWSR1-FLI1-dependent enhancer activity of this sequence, with epigenetic characteristics of an active regulatory element.

evidence.reference_title: Chimeric EWSR1-FLI1 regulates the Ewing sarcoma susceptibility gene EGR2 via a GGAA microsatellite.
evidence.snippet: EWSR1-FLI1 preferentially bound to the A risk allele, which increased global and allele-specific EGR2 expression.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted long-read sequencing of the Ewing sarcoma 6p25.1 susceptibility locus identifies germline-somatic interactions with EWSR1-FLI1 binding.
evidence.snippet: We identified 50 microsatellite alleles at 6p25.1 and observed that EwS-affected individuals had longer alleles (>135 bp) with more GGAA repeats.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted long-read sequencing of the Ewing sarcoma 6p25.1 susceptibility locus identifies germline-somatic interactions with EWSR1-FLI1 binding.
evidence.snippet: RREB1 knockdown reduced proliferation and clonogenic potential and reduced expression of cell cycle and DNA replication genes.

nodes.description: Fusion-created enhancer activity at the HOXD locus induces a developmental transcriptional program. HOXD13 activates some genes normally repressed by EWS-FLI1 and shifts cells toward mesenchymal and migratory states. This provides a defined modifier of the differentiation block and contributes to a continuum of tumor states.

evidence.reference_title: EWS::FLI1 and HOXD13 Control Tumor Cell Plasticity in Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: We found that EWS::FLI1 creates a de novo GGAA microsatellite enhancer in a developmentally conserved regulatory region of the HOXD locus.

evidence.reference_title: EWS::FLI1 and HOXD13 Control Tumor Cell Plasticity in Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: More strikingly, HOXD13 bound and activated EWS::FLI1-repressed genes, leading to adoption of mesenchymal and migratory cell states that are normally suppressed by the fusion.

nodes.description: Early human embryonic mesenchymal stem cells transduced with EWS-FLI1 acquire an Ewing-like transcriptome. Tumor formation was tested separately in immunodeficient xenograft hosts. This engineered permissiveness differs from later MSC states tested in the study; it does not uniquely identify the human lineage of origin.
nodes.id: Human embryonic mesenchymal stem cell EWS-FLI1 transformation model

evidence.reference_title: EWS::FLI1 expression in human embryonic mesenchymal stem cells leads to transcriptional reprograming, defective DNA damage repair and Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: In summary, we show that EWS::FLI1 enforces an aberrant transcriptome and solely is able to endow transforming capacity when expressed in undifferentiated, early heMSCs.

nodes.description: Ewing tumors contain coexisting gene-regulatory programs. CD73-positive malignant subpopulations can retain fusion-activated genes while expressing normally repressed mesenchymal and extracellular-matrix genes. These CAF-like tumor cells deposit matrix near tumor borders and invasive foci. Their presence is not proof of a separate fibroblast lineage, and a universal binary fusion-high/fusion-low switch does not capture the observed heterogeneity.
nodes.id: Hybrid Mesenchymal Tumor States and Matrix Deposition

evidence.reference_title: Multimodal single-cell analyses reveal distinct fusion-regulated transcriptional programs in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: When we examined primary EwS patient tumors, we observed these same regulatory modules were variably enriched both across and within tumors, highlighting the existence of intratumoral heterogeneity in gene regulatory networks.

evidence.reference_title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Like Tumor Cells Remodel the Ewing Sarcoma Tumor Microenvironment.
evidence.snippet: These cells retained expression of the fusion-activated gene signature alongside high expression of genes that are normally repressed by EWS::FLI1.

evidence.reference_title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Like Tumor Cells Remodel the Ewing Sarcoma Tumor Microenvironment.
evidence.snippet: Thus, these EwS cells gained mesenchymal properties, including the capacity to deposit ECM, without losing proliferative or tumorigenic potential.

nodes.description: Transient IGF-1 exposure at concentrations chosen to mimic pubertal serum levels reprogrammed limb-derived mesenchymal cells from EWS-FLI1-mutant mice through a YAP1-centered mechanism and enabled stable tumorigenicity. This model suggests a developmental cooperating signal but does not establish puberty as the time of human initiation, a universal IGF-1 requirement, or a human cell of origin. YAP1/TAZ can oppose fusion transcription while promoting aggressive behavior in established tumors, so initiation and maintenance contexts require separate testing.

biological_processes: insulin-like growth factor receptor signaling pathway

evidence.reference_title: YAP1 is a key regulator of EWS::FLI1-dependent malignant transformation upon IGF-1-mediated reprogramming of bone mesenchymal stem cells.
evidence.snippet: We report that transient exposure to IGF-1 concentrations mimicking serum levels during puberty reprograms limb-derived mesenchymal cells of EWS::FLI1-mutant mice to stable transformation and tumorigenicity.

evidence.reference_title: YAP1 is a key regulator of EWS::FLI1-dependent malignant transformation upon IGF-1-mediated reprogramming of bone mesenchymal stem cells.
evidence.snippet: We identify a modular mechanism of IGF-1-driven tumor promotion in the early steps of EwS pathogenesis, in which Yap1 plays a central role.

nodes.description: Seclidemstat (SP-2577) is an investigational LSD1-associated transcriptional modulator studied in fusion-positive sarcoma cells and trials. Laboratory activity links to fusion-dependent transcription, but clinical efficacy in Ewing sarcoma is unproven and preclinical xenograft activity has been limited.

evidence.reference_title: Seclidemstat (SP-2577) Induces Transcriptomic Reprogramming and Cytotoxicity in Multiple Fusion-Positive Sarcomas.
evidence.snippet: Seclidemstat recapitulated much of SP-2509 transcriptional activity in Ewing sarcoma.

evidence.reference_title: In vivo evaluation of the lysine-specific demethylase (KDM1A/LSD1) inhibitor SP-2577 (Seclidemstat) against pediatric sarcoma preclinical models: A report from the Pediatric Preclinical Testing Consortium (PPTC).
evidence.snippet: SP-2577 (100 mg/kg/day × 28 days) statistically significantly (p < .05) inhibited growth of three of eight Ewing sarcoma (EwS), four of five rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS), and four of six osteosarcoma (OS) xenografts.

nodes.description: About one quarter of patients have detectable metastases at diagnosis, predominantly in lung, bone and bone marrow. Prognosis depends on metastatic distribution, age and treatment. In the metastatic AEWS1221 trial, three-year event-free survival was 37.4% with VDC/IE and 39.1% with added ganitumab; these estimates are not five-year overall survival.

evidence.reference_title: Outcomes of Adult Ewing Sarcoma Treated with Multimodality Therapy: A Single-Institute Experience.
evidence.snippet: Among 21 (28.8%) patients, the lung (61.9%) was the most common site of metastasis followed by the bone, bone marrow, and brain.

evidence.reference_title: Randomized Phase III Trial of Ganitumab With Interval-Compressed Chemotherapy for Patients With Newly Diagnosed Metastatic Ewing Sarcoma: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group.
evidence.snippet: The 3-year EFS estimates were 37.4% (95% CI, 29.3 to 45.5) for the standard arm and 39.1% (95% CI, 31.3 to 46.7) for the experimental arm (stratified EFS-event hazard ratio for experimental arm 1.00; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.33; 1-sided, P = .50).

evidence.reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of Ewing sarcoma (Spanish Sarcoma Research Group-GEIS).
evidence.snippet: Although only 25% of patients have obvious metastases at diagnosis

nodes.description: Lineage-targeted fusion expression produced neural crest-to-mesoderm reprogramming and lethal Ewing-like tumors. This establishes origin and reprogramming within the zebrafish model, not definitive ancestry of human tumors.

evidence.reference_title: Origin of Ewing sarcoma by embryonic reprogramming of neural crest to mesoderm.
evidence.snippet: Neural crest-derived cells uniquely tolerate expression of EWSR1::FLI1, and targeted expression of EWSR1::FLI1 in these cells generates lethal Ewing sarcomas.

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1 recruits NuRD-associated HDAC and LSD1 activities to repress tumor-suppressive and lineage-regulatory genes. Repression contributes to transformation alongside enhancer activation. CHD4 also maintains global chromatin architecture and survival, but this distinct dependency should not be equated with regulation of EWS-FLI1 transcriptional output.

biological_processes: negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

evidence.reference_title: Mechanism and relevance of EWS/FLI-mediated transcriptional repression in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistic studies demonstrate that the NuRD co-repressor complex interacts with EWS/FLI, and that its associated histone deacetylase and LSD1 activities contribute to the repressive function.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanism and relevance of EWS/FLI-mediated transcriptional repression in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that a previously less-well characterized transcriptional repressive function of the EWS/FLI fusion is also required for the transformed phenotype of Ewing sarcoma.

nodes.description: In osseous Ewing sarcoma, infiltrative tumor growth destroys the affected bone and can extend through cortex into soft tissue. Local structural injury contributes to pain, swelling and fracture risk. These consequences are specific to osseous or bone-involving disease; treatment can also contribute to later fractures.
nodes.id: Osseous Tumor Expansion and Bone Destruction

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and treatment of Ewing sarcoma of the bone: a review article.
evidence.snippet: In ES of the bone, plain radiographs exhibit permeative and infiltrative destruction of the affected bone

nodes.description: PARP-inhibitor combinations remain investigational in recurrent/refractory Ewing sarcoma. Talazoparib plus temozolomide produced no objective responses in ten phase-2 Ewing patients. A later pediatric olaparib-irinotecan phase-I/II study reported two Ewing responses, with a 6.3% response rate in its evaluable Ewing cohort. These limited signals do not establish routine efficacy or a validated HR-deficiency biomarker.

evidence.reference_title: Phase 1/2 trial of talazoparib in combination with temozolomide in children and adolescents with refractory/recurrent solid tumors including Ewing sarcoma: A Children's Oncology Group Phase 1 Consortium study (ADVL1411).
evidence.snippet: In phase 2, 0 of 10 EWS subjects experienced an objective response; two experienced prolonged SD.

evidence.reference_title: Phase I/II Study of the PARP Inhibitor Olaparib and Irinotecan in Children and Young Adults with Recurrent/Refractory Malignancies: Arm D of the AcSé-ESMART Trial.
evidence.snippet: Two patients with Ewing sarcoma experienced a complete and a partial response for 10 and 42 cycles, respectively.

nodes.description: PARP1 interacts with EWS-FLI1 and EWS-ERG and supports fusion-mediated transcription; EWS-FLI1 also maintains PARP1 expression. This experimentally reported feedback connects transcription and damage response. The preclinical drug rationale has not translated into uniform clinical response.

evidence.reference_title: PARP-1 inhibition as a targeted strategy to treat Ewing's sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Notably, EWS-FLI1 fusion genes acted in a positive feedback loop to maintain the expression of PARP1, which was required for EWS-FLI-mediated transcription, thereby enforcing oncogene-dependent sensitivity to PARP-1 inhibition.

nodes.description: Fractures can complicate osseous Ewing sarcoma at presentation or during and after treatment. A historical long-bone cohort reported fractures in 14/93 patients across the disease course, including many after radiation; this is not a disease-wide presentation frequency.

evidence.reference_title: Fractures in pediatric Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Fracture occurred in 14 (15%) of 93 patients with long-bone ESFT, most commonly in the femur.

evidence.reference_title: Fractures in pediatric Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Nine (64%) of the 14 fractures occurred after the start of radiotherapy, and three of these were associated with either local recurrence or second malignancy.

nodes.description: Patient-derived Ewing sarcoma cultures provide a primary-cell in vitro non-animal model for studying EWSR1 fusion status, proliferation, migration, and treatment response in models that differ transcriptionally from long-established cell lines.

evidence.reference_title: Characterisation of Bespoke Patient-Derived In Vitro Models of Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: To expedite this process, we have established and characterised patient-derived ES cultures (PDES) in vitro.

nodes.description: The human cell of origin remains unresolved. Human neural crest-derived stem cells can tolerate EWS-FLI1, and early human embryonic mesenchymal cells can acquire an Ewing-like program and form xenografts. A zebrafish genetic model demonstrates neural crest-to-mesoderm reprogramming and tumors after lineage-targeted fusion expression. These experiments identify permissive states in distinct systems; neither molecular similarity nor engineered transformation uniquely traces the origin of human tumors.

animal_models.description: Tests lineage-specific fusion tolerance and transformation.
animal_models.name: Neural-crest-targeted EWSR1-FLI1 zebrafish

animal_models.description: Tests tumorigenicity of an experimentally permissive progenitor state.
animal_models.genotype: Immunodeficient hosts xenografted with EWS::FLI1-transduced human embryonic MSCs
animal_models.name: EWS-FLI1-transduced human embryonic MSC xenograft

evidence.reference_title: Modeling initiation of Ewing sarcoma in human neural crest cells.
evidence.snippet: Although the histogenesis of ESFT is controversial, mesenchymal (MSC) and/or neural crest (NCSC) stem cells have been implicated as cells of origin.

evidence.reference_title: Modeling initiation of Ewing sarcoma in human neural crest cells.
evidence.snippet: Together these studies confirm that, unlike terminally differentiated cells but consistent with bone marrow-derived MSC, NCSC tolerate expression of EWS-FLI1 and ectopic expression of the oncogene initiates transition to an ESFT-like state.

evidence.reference_title: EWS::FLI1 expression in human embryonic mesenchymal stem cells leads to transcriptional reprograming, defective DNA damage repair and Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Ewing sarcoma (ES) is an aggressive bone and soft tissue neoplasm characterized by EWSR::ETS rearrangements whose cellular origin remains unclear.

evidence.reference_title: EWS::FLI1 expression in human embryonic mesenchymal stem cells leads to transcriptional reprograming, defective DNA damage repair and Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Xenografting of EWS::FLI1-transduced heMSCs results in the formation of tumors expressing characteristic ES markers.

evidence.reference_title: Origin of Ewing sarcoma by embryonic reprogramming of neural crest to mesoderm.
evidence.snippet: Neural crest-derived cells uniquely tolerate expression of EWSR1::FLI1, and targeted expression of EWSR1::FLI1 in these cells generates lethal Ewing sarcomas.

experimental_models.description: Demonstrates that only undifferentiated, early heMSCs (not adult MSCs or pediatric MSCs) fully support EWS-FLI1 transformation, linking progenitor developmental state to oncogenic permissiveness.
experimental_models.name: Human embryonic mesenchymal stem cell EWS-FLI1 transformation model

nodes.description: A 2025 bioRxiv preprint reports that EWS-FLI1 expression or EWSR1 loss induces POLQ exon 25 skipping, reduces polymerase theta protein, and impairs microhomology-mediated end joining. Fusion knockdown and POLQ rescue support causality in tested models. Proposed synthetic lethality with other repair pathways requires independent replication and clinical evaluation; this is an emerging additional repair defect rather than a reason to erase the BRCA1 literature.
nodes.id: Proposed POLQ Splicing and MMEJ Defect

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of Microhomology-mediated End-joining in Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Expression of EWS-FLI1, or loss of EWSR1, causes exon 25 skipping of the POLQ transcript, decreased POLΘ expression, impaired MMEJ, and cellular sensitivity to inhibitors of the Fanconi Anemia (FA), NHEJ, or HR pathways, through the mechanism of synthetic lethality.

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1 directly increases SLFN11 expression. SLFN11 blocks stressed replication forks and promotes susceptibility to DNA-damaging agents. Expression-outcome correlations are not a validated standalone clinical selection test. Loss of SLFN11 can confer treatment resistance and is associated with metabolic adaptation in Ewing models.

evidence.reference_title: SLFN11 Is a Transcriptional Target of EWS-FLI1 and a Determinant of Drug Response in Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: EWS-FLI1 binds near the transcription start site of SLFN11 promoter and acts as a positive regulator of SLFN11 expression in Ewing sarcoma cells.

evidence.reference_title: SLFN11 Blocks Stressed Replication Forks Independently of ATR.
evidence.snippet: Unlike ATR, SLFN11 neither interferes with the loading of CDC45 and PCNA nor inhibits the initiation of DNA replication but selectively blocks fork progression while inducing chromatin opening across replication initiation sites.

nodes.description: SLFN11-deficient Ewing models show reduced GPD2 expression and increased glycerophospholipid biosynthesis. Pharmacologic inhibition of glycerophospholipid synthesis increased SN-38 sensitivity in vitro, with modest and cell-line-dependent combination effects. The regulatory link from SLFN11 loss to GPD2 suppression and human predictive value remain unresolved. This loss state is not represented as a positive consequence of SLFN11 fork arrest.

evidence.reference_title: Targeting glycerophospholipid biosynthesis overcomes chemoresistance driven by SLFN11 loss in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Here, we leverage transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling in patient-derived EWS models to demonstrate that SLFN11 loss drives downregulated mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GPD2) expression, higher accumulation of glycerol-3-phosphate, fatty acid unsaturation, and enhanced glycerophospholipid (GPL) biosynthesis.

evidence.reference_title: Genomic landscape of Ewing sarcoma defines an aggressive subtype with co-association of STAG2 and TP53 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Apart from whole chromosome arm copy-number changes, the most common somatic mutations were detected in STAG2 (17%), CDKN2A (12%), TP53 (7%), EZH2, BCOR, and ZMYM3 (2.7% each).

evidence.reference_title: Adverse prognostic impact of the loss of STAG2 protein expression in patients with newly diagnosed localised Ewing sarcoma: A report from the Children's Oncology Group.
evidence.snippet: Among patients with localised disease, 5-year event-free survival was 54% (95% CI 34-70%) and 75% (95% CI 63-84%) for patients with STAG2 loss vs. expression (P = 0.0034).

nodes.description: STAG2 loss remodels cohesin-dependent enhancer-promoter and CTCF contacts and perturbs PRC2-regulated programs in a subset of Ewing tumors. A recent study found loss of many short-GGAA binding sites with increased fusion occupancy and activity at multimeric repeats. Earlier work showed that STAG2 normally facilitates long-GGAA enhancer contacts; this is related evidence, not an independent replication of the same directional occupancy change. STAG2 protein loss and STAG2/TP53 co-mutation associate with adverse outcome in specific cohorts, but mutation, protein loss and inferred chromatin states are not interchangeable biomarkers.

evidence.reference_title: STAG2 loss rewires oncogenic and developmental programs to promote metastasis in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Strikingly, in STAG2 knockout cells the oncogenic genetic program driven by the fusion transcription factor EWS/FLI1 was highly perturbed, in part due to altered enhancer-promoter contacts. Moreover, loss of STAG2 also disrupted PRC2-mediated regulation of gene expression.

evidence.reference_title: STAG2 loss rewires oncogenic and developmental programs to promote metastasis in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Finally, consistent with clinical observations, functional studies revealed that loss of STAG2 enhances the metastatic potential of Ewing sarcoma xenografts.

evidence.reference_title: STAG2 loss amplifies EWS-FLI1-driven microsatellite enhancer activity promoting Ewing sarcoma aggressiveness.
evidence.snippet: Together, these findings reveal that STAG2 loss reprograms, rather than globally attenuates, EWS-FLI1 function, amplifying a high-risk oncogenic transcriptional state in Ewing sarcoma.

evidence.reference_title: STAG2 loss in Ewing sarcoma alters enhancer-promoter contacts dependent and independent of EWS::FLI1.
evidence.snippet: Subsequent genomic profiling and high-resolution chromatin interaction data from Capture Hi-C indicated that cohesin-STAG2 facilitates communication between EWS::FLI1-bound long GGAA repeats, presumably acting as neoenhancers, and their target promoters.

evidence.reference_title: STAG2 loss in Ewing sarcoma alters enhancer-promoter contacts dependent and independent of EWS::FLI1.
evidence.snippet: Changes in CTCF-dependent chromatin contacts involving signature genes, unrelated to EWS::FLI1 binding, were also identified.

evidence.reference_title: Adverse prognostic impact of the loss of STAG2 protein expression in patients with newly diagnosed localised Ewing sarcoma: A report from the Children's Oncology Group.
evidence.snippet: Among patients with localised disease, 5-year event-free survival was 54% (95% CI 34-70%) and 75% (95% CI 63-84%) for patients with STAG2 loss vs. expression (P = 0.0034).

evidence.reference_title: Genomic landscape of Ewing sarcoma defines an aggressive subtype with co-association of STAG2 and TP53 mutations.
evidence.snippet: In an expanded cohort of 299 patients with clinical data, we discovered that STAG2 and TP53 mutations are often concurrent and are associated with poor outcome.

nodes.description: A palpable mass or localized swelling may develop as tumor extends through the bone cortex into surrounding soft tissues. The mass is often firm and may be tender or warm, and may initially be attributed to trauma or infection.

evidence.reference_title: Outcomes of Adult Ewing Sarcoma Treated with Multimodality Therapy: A Single-Institute Experience.
evidence.snippet: In this study, pain and swelling were the most common presenting complaints seen in 75.3% and 42.5% patients, respectively

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1-driven transcription and impaired regulation of damage-induced transcription promote RNA:DNA hybrids and replication stress in Ewing cell models. The stress state creates DNA-damage vulnerabilities and dependence on buffering pathways. It does not itself cause enhanced survival, and it is not synonymous with a uniform BRCA-mutant clinical phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: EWS-FLI1 increases transcription to cause R-loops and block BRCA1 repair in Ewing sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that Ewing sarcoma cells display alterations in regulation of damage-induced transcription, accumulation of R-loops and increased replication stress.

nodes.description: Multiple fusion-driven mechanisms converge on tumor cell proliferation and survival: core regulatory circuitry sustains oncogenic signaling, metabolic reprogramming supplies biomass and redox buffering, and replication-stress adaptation prevents apoptosis during genotoxic stress.

experimental_models.description: Enables preclinical testing of tumor growth and survival responses.
experimental_models.name: Ewing sarcoma tumor organoid model systems

experimental_models.description: Assays patient-derived proliferation and therapy-response phenotypes.
experimental_models.name: Patient-derived Ewing sarcoma culture panel

experimental_models.description: Models stromal support of growth and drug-resistance phenotypes.
experimental_models.name: Flow-perfusion Ewing sarcoma 3D scaffold coculture

nodes.description: In flow-perfusion coculture, mesenchymal stromal cells and Ewing tumor cells respond to biophysical cues through IL-6/STAT3 signaling and altered drug response. This established-tumor microenvironment mechanism is distinct from IGF-1/YAP1 developmental initiation.

evidence.reference_title: Modeling Stroma-Induced Drug Resistance in a Tissue-Engineered Tumor Model of Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that these same biophysical cues-modeled by coculturing ES cells and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in 3D scaffolds within a flow perfusion bioreactor-activate interleukin-6 and transcription factor Stat3.

experimental_models.description: Assays IL-6/STAT3 tumor-stroma signaling and drug response under biophysical stimulation; it does not test developmental IGF-1/YAP1 initiation.
experimental_models.name: Flow-perfusion Ewing sarcoma 3D scaffold coculture

nodes.description: USP1 inhibition is a preclinical targeted strategy aimed at the EWS-FLI1 induced USP1-survivin survival buffer that helps Ewing sarcoma cells tolerate endogenous replication stress and standard chemotherapy exposure.

evidence.reference_title: USP1 Expression Driven by EWS::FLI1 Transcription Factor Stabilizes Survivin and Mitigates Replication Stress in Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: USP1 knockdown or inhibition arrests EWS cell growth and induces cell death by apoptosis.

nodes.description: EWS-FLI1 increases USP1 expression. USP1 stabilizes survivin and buffers replication-stress-associated apoptosis, allowing continued Ewing cell survival. USP1 inhibition sensitizes cells to doxorubicin and etoposide in preclinical experiments; human efficacy has not been established.

evidence.reference_title: USP1 Expression Driven by EWS::FLI1 Transcription Factor Stabilizes Survivin and Mitigates Replication Stress in Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Together, our study demonstrates that USP1 is regulated by EWS::FLI1, the USP1-Survivin axis promotes EWS cell survival, and USP1 inhibition sensitizes cells to standard of care chemotherapy.
